title: Representation learning of human cortical folding to reveal long lasting neurodevelopmental signatures
abstract: arXiv:2609.05438v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The human brain folds in utero, primarily during late gestation. Shortly after birth, cortical folding patterns are established and remain stable thereafter, making them promising early neurodevelopmental markers. Yet it is unclear whether representations given by current neuroimaging foundation models capture cortical folding variability. Here, we introduce Champollion, a self-supervised learning framework that learns interpretable local representations of cortical folding from structural MRI. Optimized on representative folding-related tasks, Champollion accurately captures known folding patterns across cortical regions and external datasets. In a comprehensive benchmark, it consistently outperforms neuroimaging and general-purpose foundation models. Furthermore, Champollion reveals richer genetic associations than conventional morphometric descriptors and identifies localized folding signatures associated with incomplete hippocampal

translated_title: 人类大脑皮层折叠的表征学习以揭示持久的神经发育特征
translated_abstract: 人类大脑在子宫内发生折叠，主要发生在妊娠晚期。出生后不久，皮层折叠模式即已确立并在此后保持稳定，使其成为极具前景的早期神经发育标志物。然而，目前尚不清楚现有神经影像基础模型所提供的表征能否捕捉皮层折叠的变异性。在此，我们提出Champollion，一个自监督学习框架，可从结构磁共振成像中学习可解释的皮层折叠局部表征。通过在代表性折叠相关任务上进行优化，Champollion能够准确捕捉跨皮层区域和外部数据集的已知折叠模式。在一项全面的基准测试中，它始终优于神经影像基础模型和通用基础模型。此外，Champollion揭示了比传统形态计量描述符更丰富的遗传关联，并识别出与海马不完全……相关的局部折叠特征。
tldr: 本文提出自监督学习框架Champollion，能从结构MRI中学习可解释的皮层折叠局部表征，其性能超越现有神经影像及通用基础模型，并揭示出比传统形态学指标更丰富的遗传关联和持久的神经发育特征。
en_tdlr: We introduce Champollion, a self-supervised learning framework that learns interpretable local representations of cortical folding from structural MRI, consistently outperforming neuroimaging and general-purpose foundation models while revealing richer genetic associations and long-lasting neurodevelopmental signatures.
